title: Stratified finite coefficient models for the all-continuous algebraic closure
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the topology of the extended $\ell$-adic absolute value, and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Put $B(S)=C(S,\Omega)$ on profinite sets, with all continuous maps, and $A_E(S)=C(S,E)$ for a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$ with its restricted norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $B_T=p_T^*B$ and $A_{E,T}=p_T^*A_E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The continuous inclusion $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ gives the coefficient map $A_{E,T}\to B_T$ by postcomposition and pullback [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Modules are internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For every scheme $T$ and every $B_T$-module $M$ with finite constant local models on a finite constructible stratification [sk-def-sfb-constructible, det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], there is a finite partition $T=\coprod_{a=1}^r T_a$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], a finite extension $E_a/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Omega$ for each $a$, and a lisse $A_{E_a,T_a}$-module $L_a$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] such that
$$B_{T_a}\otimes_{A_{E_a,T_a}}L_a\ \cong\ M|_{T_a}.$$
Here tensor is ordinary extension of internal module scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The stratification may refine the given one; neither a model for $M$ over one field on all of $T$ nor finite-subextension-valued coefficient sections are required. Empty $T$, zero modules and rank zero are included.

source.place: Paragraph (3), all-continuous compatibility obligation: finite coefficient models on source strata before applying open-image finiteness Agent-stated coefficient-specific input, not an identification with the filtered-union coefficient.

proof.text: Let $T=\coprod S_b$ be the given finite constructible stratification. On every member of the given trivializing cover of $S_b$, its scalar model $P$ is a finitely presented $\Omega$-module. Since $\Omega$ is a field, finite generation gives a finite basis, say $P\cong\Omega^n$. The functor $P\mapsto B_U\otimes_{\Omega}P$ sends this basis to the $n$ standard generators: $b\otimes(a_i)_i\mapsto(ba_i)_i$, with inverse $(b_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i b_i\otimes e_i$. Thus the same cover exhibits $M|_{S_b}$ as lisse. This uses the scalar-ring and finite-constant-model conventions of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] and the definition [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], and admits $n=0$.

source.place: Paragraphs (1)–(3): field-valued local models; agent linear-algebra expansion

proof.text: The scheme $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has only the ideals $0,k$). Its closed subsets satisfy the minimal condition [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. Each original stratum $S_b$ and each reduced closed subscheme of it is again finite type over $k$: on affine charts a closed subscheme is a quotient of a finitely generated $k$-algebra, generated by the images of the same generators; open subsets are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], their inclusions are finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and finite type composes by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. These observations also apply to the successive reduced closed complements below. Separatedness is inherited by subschemes since their diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal. We now refine each $S_b$ into normal integral locally closed subschemes by the explicit Noetherian induction in the next step.

source.place: Tag 01OZ, lemma-Noetherian-topology; agent preparation for Noetherian induction

proof.text: Fix one $S_b$, the image of the immersion $Z_b\to T$ of the given stratification; by definition [def-weil-closed-immersion] it is a closed immersion $Z_b\to O_b$ followed by the inclusion of an open $O_b\subseteq T$. Induct on the closed subsets $F$ of $|Z_b|$, with the claim that $F$ is a finite disjoint union of locally closed subsets, each with a normal integral scheme structure immersed onto it in $T$. The empty subset has the empty partition. For nonempty $F$, its irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ are finitely many, cover it [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components, lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] and are closed in $Z_b$. Give $C_i$ its reduced induced structure in $Z_b$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; it is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The open $C_i^\circ=C_i\setminus\bigcup_{j\neq i}C_j$ of $F$ is nonempty by maximality of $C_i$, integral as an open subscheme of $C_i$, and of finite type over $k$ by Step 2; [lem-fin-dense-normal-open] gives a nonempty normal open $V_i\subseteq C_i^\circ$. The $V_i$ are disjoint, open in $F$ and dense in $C_i$, so the complement $F'$ of their union is a proper closed subset. Apply the inductive hypothesis to $F'$ and append the $V_i$; the minimal condition of Step 2 validates the induction. $C_i\to Z_b\to O_b$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]; $V_i=C_i\cap W_i$ for an open $W_i\subseteq O_b$, and $V_i\to W_i$ is a closed immersion, since over each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq W_i$ it is that of $C_i\to O_b$, of the form $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. So $V_i\to T$ is an immersion through $Z_b$. The pieces are constructible as $T$ is Noetherian [def-weil-constructible-subset], and form the required refining stratification [def-constructible-stratification]. Each is integral, hence irreducible and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], normal, Noetherian and separated by Step 2.

source.place: Paragraph (3): agent normal-stratum refinement using the existing dense normal open lemma

proof.text: Let $S$ be a nonempty piece just constructed and put $N=M|_S$. Pull back the cover and finite free models of Step 1 to $S$. Pullback transports the coefficient ring to $B_S$ and the regular module to its regular module, and commutes with finite sums; this follows directly from the strong monoidal inverse image and the module pullback formula [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Consequently $N$ is lisse by [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Choose a geometric point of $S$ (an algebraic closure of the residue field of any point defines one). Apply [lem-sfb-normal-continuous-algcl-monodromy] with $K=\Omega$. Its hypotheses hold because $S$ is normal, connected, Noetherian and separated, and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ is invertible on $S$. It identifies $N$ with a continuous representation on $\Omega^n$ for a finite $n$.

source.place: Section 7.4, pp. 70–71, with the coefficient-specific strengthening isolated in the cited new node

proof.text: Write $\rho:\Pi\to\operatorname{GL}_n(\Omega)$ for this representation, with $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(S,\bar s)$. Compose with the multiplicative inclusion into square matrices. The group $\Pi$ is profinite, hence compact, and every matrix entry is continuous by the preceding monodromy statement. Apply [lem-real-compact-matrix-coefficient-descent] with $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. It gives a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ containing every entry of $\rho(g)$ for every $g$. This use concerns a compact group homomorphism, rather than an arbitrary compact set of coefficient values.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, p. 3, first bullet: finite coefficient descent for compact monodromy

proof.text: Regard the same matrices as a representation $\rho_E$ on $E^n$. They are invertible over $E$ because the entries of $\rho(g^{-1})$ also belong to $E$ and the identities $\rho(g)\rho(g^{-1})=1=\rho(g^{-1})\rho(g)$ hold over that subfield. The coordinate functions to $E$ are continuous: for the subspace topology on $E\subseteq\Omega$, a function already valued in $E$ is continuous precisely when its composite with the inclusion is continuous. The inverse equivalence $\Phi_E$ of [lem-sfb-normal-continuous-algcl-monodromy] gives a lisse $A_{E,S}$-module $L$. Its coefficient comparison is for exactly the postcomposition and pullback map in the item. Under that comparison, $B_S\otimes_{A_{E,S}}L$ corresponds to $\Omega\otimes_E E^n$. The basis map $a\otimes(v_i)_i\mapsto(av_i)_i$ is an equivariant isomorphism to $\Omega^n$ with action $\rho$; its inverse sends $(w_i)_i$ to $\sum_i w_i\otimes e_i$. Full faithfulness of $\Phi_\Omega$ gives $B_S\otimes_{A_{E,S}}L\cong N$. No derived tensor or flatness assertion is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3): agent finite-field representation model and its explicit scalar-extension identification

proof.text: Perform Steps 4–6 independently on the finitely many normal pieces and write their outputs as $(E_a,L_a)$. Their stratification refines the original one by the factorizations in Step 3, and their isomorphisms are exactly the displayed isomorphisms of the item. On an empty $T$ choose the empty stratification. For a zero module the same argument uses $n=0$; one may choose $E_a=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $L_a=0$. There is no gluing across different strata, and no requirement to put arbitrary continuous $\Omega$-valued functions inside a finite coefficient field.

My own truth check of the new node lem-sfb-normal-continuous-algcl-monodromy: push the torsor out to GL_n(C_l), which is Noohi (its O-points are a limit of discrete groups), so Pi profinite gives a monodromy map and a trivialisation on the universal pro-finite-etale cover. The Omega-reduction is constant on that irreducible cover, because every component of a w-contractible cover meets the generic fibre. The cocycle is then a continuous Pi -> GL_n(Omega), which lands in GL_n(E) by Baire. Small cases pass: Spec F_q, a geometric point, rank 0. I judge it true, and strictly smaller than the item (no stratification, no finite-field claim).
